pr_title: sql: fix sql activity job from adding too many rows
pr_body:
The SQL activity update job runs every 10 minutes. It always upserts the new rows into the statement_activity and transaction_activity table.

The problem is if a customer uses an ORM where it generates a lot of unique queries then the job will keep adding new rows. This causes the activity tables to grow very large. One customer had over 58k rows for a single hour. This causes the SQL Activity page to be very slow.

To prevent the table from growing the update is now done in a transaction where the first statement deletes all the rows, and the next inserts the new rows computed from the statistic table. It needs to be done in a single transaction to avoid user getting no results during the upgrade process. It also ensures that if the job fails it only deletes the older rows if inserting the new rows succeeds.

Epic: none
Fixes: #104169

Release note (sql change): Fixes the SQL Activity update job, so the
 statement_activity and transaction_activity table size is constrained
 when customer has a lot of unique queries. The prevents the SQL
 Activity page from becoming slow.

issue_context.title: sql activity: sql activity update job adding too many rows
issue_context.body:
The sql activity update job should only be adding the top 500 for each of the 6 cached columns which should put it at 3k rows per an hour. A user reported the system.statement_activity having more than 58k rows in a single hour. 

The user had over 100k rows per an hour in the system.statement_statistics so a lot of fingerprints are being generated.

Possible causes:
1. ORM is generating a lot of unique fingerprints. Each time job runs it's upserting a new top 500. Currently no work is done to remove queries no longer in the top 500 to keep overhead to a minimum.
2. User is setting unique name per query execution.

Solution:
1. In the cleanup function add a check to remove any queries not in the top 500 for the 6 columns.
2. On update delete all previous rows for that hour and then insert all new top 500.

Jira issue: CRDB-28382

review_comments: Curious, is this going to cause noticeable contentiom when we are attempting to read the sql activity tables via the UI and this job is modifying the table? Also do you think it would be worthwhile to run the stmt and txn table txns concurrently?
